text: Evidence shows that the type of dietary fat consumed has a direct influence on body composition. Rosqvist and colleagues (117) demonstrated that overfeeding young men and women of normal weight with foods high in n -6 fatty acids caused an approximately 3-fold increase in lean tissue mass compared to comparable overfeeding with saturated fats. It is conceivable that results were related to differential effects on cell membrane fluidity between the types of fats consumed. Specifically, PUFAs have been shown to enhance the fluidity of the membrane, whereas SFAs have the opposite effect (96). Cell membranes serve a critical role in regulating the passage of nutrients, hormones, and chemical signals into and out of cells. When membranes harden, they are desensitized to external stimuli,
